description: GFPLAIN250m, a global high-resolution dataset of Earth’s floodplains is a data set described in a peer-reviewed Scientific Data article written by F. Nardi et al. Identifying floodplain boundaries is used in earth, environmental and socioeconomic studies addressing riverine risk and resource management. However, to date, a global floodplain delineation using a homogeneous procedure has not been constructed. In this paper, we present the first, complete, high-resolution, gridded dataset of Earth’s floodplains at 250-m resolution (GFPLAIN250m). Coverage: global; published in 2019. Formats: GeoTIFF, TXT, Image, Raster. The data are held in Figshare and reached through its DOI listed on this page; the paper's Data Records section names it. Size stated by the repository: 81697833 Bytes. Access is free of charge and open according to the article. The licence is CC-BY-4.0, taken from DataCite rights of the deposit. Caveats: written from the Scientific Data article metadata (title, abstract, Data Records section) read on 2026-10-01; the data themselves were not opened or downloaded, so their contents, quality and current availability were not checked. It can support multi-sector infrastructure risk and planning studies. Related records: none catalogued yet.
